answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by forcing each identity up an escalation ladder: reputation compounds along a spiral of verified history, where every rung is a graded original contribution. Each fake must reach a costly vertex of trust - enough attested references - before it earns anything, so mass forgery means mass payment. The system also checks the fable: claims must match behavior, so no fabricated backstory passes. Cost per fake stays high, reward stays zero until proven, and the spiral makes cutting in expensive.
